title: Signal Hill
synopsis: On the last night before the old radio array is scrapped, a satellite that appears in no registry begins transmitting a countdown — and, patiently, your name.

nodes.text: You are the only operator left on the hill the night before they decommission the array. At 00:00 a carrier wave arrives from a satellite that exists in no catalog you can find. It ticks down — twelve, eleven, ten — one number an hour. Between the numbers, in clean Morse, it spells your name.

choices.text: Log it and wake the chain of command
choices.consequence: You log it and wake the chain of command. The path to The Chain of Command opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Answer it yourself, off the record
choices.consequence: You commit to answer it yourself, off the record. It carries you toward Your Own Voice, Returned, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: The duty supervisor answers on the third ring, unhappy. "It's a ghost harmonic off the old relay. Stand down, log it, go home." You hang up. The count reaches nine. Your name arrives again, tapped out with something that is either patience or affection.

choices.consequence: You obey, and go home. The path to Interference, They Called It opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You stay and keep listening alone. The path to Your Own Voice, Returned opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You key the transmitter and say hello into the hiss. A pause of exactly one light-second, and then hello comes back — in your voice, but decades older, sanded down by a life you have not lived yet. It does not sound surprised to hear from you.

choices.consequence: You ask who they are. The path to A Message From Later opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Ask what the countdown is counting to
choices.consequence: You commit to ask what the countdown is counting to. It carries you toward What Zero Means, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: "I'm you," the old voice says, unbothered by how impossible that is. "Forty years on. This relay is the only thing that still bounces a signal back to a night I can pin down.

choices.consequence: You commit to believe yourself. It carries you toward The Warning, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Assume it's a hoax and trace the source
choices.consequence: You assume it's a hoax and trace the source. The path to Triangulation opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: "Zero is 08:00," the voice says. "When the crew arrives to cut the array down for scrap. After that there's no antenna on Earth aimed the right way to carry me back this far.

choices.consequence: You record everything before zero. The path to The Warning opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Pull the plug now and get some sleep
choices.consequence: You pull the plug now and get some sleep. The path to Interference, They Called It opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You run the bearings three times because the answer refuses to be sky. Every fix points down and inward — beneath the operations shed, beneath your own chair. In the corner of the floor, under forty years of linoleum, there is the seam of a hatch you have never once noticed.

choices.consequence: You commit to open the hatch. It carries you toward Under Signal Hill, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

choices.text: Flag it and wait for daylight
choices.consequence: You flag it and wait for daylight. The path to Interference, They Called It opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: "I didn't cross forty years of static to chat," the voice says, gentler now. "Tomorrow you'll be offered the transfer to the coastal station. Everyone will tell you it's the smart move. Don't take it. Stay near the people who are still alive to stay near.

choices.consequence: You choose to promise to change tomorrow. By The Transfer You Turned Down, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You ask to trade places instead. The path to Under Signal Hill opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: The hatch opens onto a small warm room that should not exist — old equipment kept alive, a single chair worn to the shape of a body, and a brass plate on the console engraved with your own initials. The countdown ticks on from a speaker in the wall. Two.

choices.text: Sit down and take the watch
choices.consequence: You choose to sit down and take the watch. By Operator, Indefinite, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Climb back out and live forward
choices.consequence: You choose to climb back out and live forward. By The Transfer You Turned Down, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: You drive home before dawn. The count reaches zero without you; the crew arrives with cutting torches at eight. In the incident log it goes down as harmonic interference, cause unknown, array retired. You take the coastal transfer that spring, and for years afterward, on quiet nights, you wonder.

You decline the coastal station without fully knowing why, and stay. You call people you had been letting drift. Nothing dramatic happens — which is, you will slowly understand, the entire point. Somewhere forty years on, a satellite that no longer needs to reach anyone goes quietly dark.

You take the chair that already fits you. The room hums; the antenna above will be scrapped by morning, but down here the signal has never depended on it. You begin the long, patient work of reaching backward — toward a younger operator, on a hill, on a night you remember perfectly.
